messages:
samir: Nightly perf job errored again while uploading traces. curl hangs on the proxy for files >1.5GB, build 802.
ci-bot: build 802 failed: upload timeout (curl exit 28)

maya: large nsys exports are expected. We should export to sqlite then zstd -19 to reduce size before upload. Also consider exporting perfetto protos where supported.
ajoshi: agree. Another option is to use aws-cli multipart (aws s3 cp) or boto3 multipart with retries instead of curl behind the proxy.

samir: proposed flow for CI:
```n
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o run.nsys --force-overwrite
nsys export --output run.sqlite run.nsys
python tools/extract_kernel_signatures.py --input run.sqlite --top 100 --out kernels.csv
python tools/make_perf_summary.py --input kernels.csv --commit $GIT --cfg "$CFG" --out perf-summary.json
zstd -19 --ultra -T0 run.sqlite -o run.sqlite.zst
aws s3 cp run.sqlite.zst s3://redwood-perf/nightly/${DATE}/${ARTIFACT} --storage-class STANDARD --only-show-errors
```n
maya: extractor should emit kernels.csv plus a tiny kernel-signature list: "name|median_ms|calls" and a separate perf-summary.json with flat fields (commit, model, batch, seq_len, tokens, median_token_ms, p90_token_ms, kernel_signatures). That keeps the dashboard diff payload tiny.
clara: we keep hitting runners without GPU drivers which causes partial nsys captures. Lock the job to a "perf-gpu" nodeSelector/toleration pool to ensure consistent hosts.
kevin: infra will provision a 2-node perf-gpu pool (A100), attach an IAM role scoped to PutObject and lifecycle management on the perf bucket. Also enable VPC endpoints for S3 to avoid proxy issues.
ajoshi: on naming: let's standardize artifacts as nightly/{YYYYMMDD}/{commit}-{model}-bs{B}-seq{S}-{gpu}.{ext}. Example: nightly/20260405/3f2a7-gpt2-bs8-seq1024-A100.run.sqlite.zst

maya: retention idea: keep raw .nsys for 7 days, sqlite.zst for 30 days, kernels.csv + perf-summary.json indefinitely. Move older sqlite.zst to glacier after 30 days.
samir: dashboard needs consecutive summaries. We'll store perf-summary.json with meta.json next to artifacts. meta.json contains docker image, GPU, commit, config. That lets dashboard group results deterministically.
perf-bot: suggestion: include a compact token latency histogram summary (buckets as CSV) and top-10 kernel medians in perf-summary.json for quick diffs.

ajoshi: implementation pointers: use aws-cli or boto3 for multipart with exponential backoff. Add a pre-upload validation that file exists and size >0. If nsys export fails, produce a small error-summary artifact so dashboard shows failed capture instead of silent gap.
clara: I'll add lifecycle rules and a bucket policy for lifecycle tagging. Also add an IAM assume-role for CI to use ephemeral creds.
kevin: after changes land, we should backfill perf-summary.json for the last 21 nights using any raw sqlite/*.nsys we still have. I'll add a backfill job in the perf pipeline.

samir: owners: @ajoshi (upload script + naming), @maya (extractors + summary schema), @clara (infra + pool + IAM), @kevin (backfill). I'll open the PRs and link tests.
ajoshi: will test against a dev bucket and share a pre-signed dev path for validation. I'll include a small harness to simulate partial exports and ensure extractor handles them. :party_parrot: \n
maya: for kernel-level investigations we should optionally export perfetto proto per-run and a small flamegraph svg; store protos short-term and keep svg in perf-summary for quick triage.
ci-bot: created PERF-412: nightly-trace-export-and-compression (assignees: ajoshi, maya)
ci-bot: created PERF-413: perf-gpu-pool-provision (assignee: clara)
samir: Thanks all. Let's iterate on the perf-summary schema in the PR — smaller payloads will make dashboard diffs snappy and reduce storage costs.
